title: Urban Planning: City Grid Challenge
description: Design your dream city by zoning residential neighborhoods, commercial districts, and green parks on a city grid! Compete against industrial sprawl to create a livable, balanced metropolis. Every stone you place teaches real urban planning concepts — from land use and zoning laws to mixed-use development and community design.
learning_objectives: Understand land use zoning: residential, commercial, industrial, and mixed-use
Learn how proximity and adjacency affect property values and quality of life
Practice strategic spatial planning and territory management
Explore the tension between community needs and industrial development
Develop skills in resource allocation and long-term city planning
Understand how green spaces and buffers improve urban livability
how_to_play: You and the AI take turns placing zones on a 9x9 city grid. You place Community Zones; the AI places Industrial Zones.
Surround empty intersections with your zones to claim that territory as your neighborhood — this is how you score points.
If you completely surround a group of Industrial Zones (no empty adjacent spaces), those zones are removed — you rezoned the area!
The Ko rule prevents you from immediately undoing a single-zone capture, keeping the game moving forward.
The game ends when both players pass consecutively, meaning neither wants to place more zones.
Your final score is your claimed territory plus captured zones. The AI gets a 6.5 point komi bonus for going second. Highest score wins!

storybook_pages.title: A City Needs a Planner
storybook_pages.text: The city council has given you a blank grid — a brand new district waiting to be designed. But there's a catch: an industrial developer is also vying for the same land. Factories, warehouses, and smokestacks threaten to overrun the area. It's up to you to zone wisely, creating vibrant neighborhoods that people actually want to live in.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: aerial view of an empty city grid with roads forming a 9x9 pattern, a young urban planner holding blueprints on one side and a factory developer on the other, bright daylight, cartoon style, colorful

storybook_pages.title: Zone by Zone
storybook_pages.text: Every zone you place matters. Residential areas need parks nearby. Commercial districts thrive on foot traffic. And if industrial zones creep too close to homes, property values plummet. Think about adjacency, buffers, and how neighborhoods connect. A great city isn't just about claiming land — it's about creating livable spaces.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: split view showing a well-planned neighborhood with houses, parks, and shops on one side, and a polluted industrial zone with factories and smoke on the other, cartoon style, educational infographic feel

storybook_pages.title: Build the Future
storybook_pages.text: As the grid fills up, the real challenge emerges: balancing growth with livability. Sometimes you need to sacrifice a small area to protect a larger neighborhood. Sometimes a bold move deep into industrial territory can reclaim an entire block. Think like a real urban planner — every decision shapes the city for generations.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.
